items.title: Sol Yaged interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000
items.q: His brother-in-law, John Hammond, was very nice and warm to me.

ctx.x: I see. What was Benny’s personality like for you?

What can I say? He was the king. He was the greatest. I don’t care what he said or didn’t say. I was happy to be in the same room with him. I used to go to all of his rehearsals, every one of his recording dates, Monk. And one day I came in late. He started at a certain time and I came in about 15, 20 minutes later because I was living in Brooklyn. He says, “Sol, you’re late,” like that he would say that to me. I felt very elated that he even said that to me. He was very nice, very gracious and warm to me. His…
You and your wife handled all your affairs for all those years.
